title: Find Peak Element
statement_short: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, find a peak element and return its index. A peak element is an element that is strictly greater than its neighbors. You must write an algorithm that runs in O(log n) time.
constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 1000, -2^31 <= nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1, nums[i] != nums[i+1] for all valid i
hint: Mandated O(log n) time complexity on unsorted arrays indicates binary search using slope comparison (nums[mid] vs nums[mid+1]).
why_not: Right: Binary Search compares mid with mid+1 to walk up the increasing slope towards a guaranteed local peak in O(log n) time. Not Two Pointers: Linear pointer scanning checks neighbor values in O(n) time, violating the strict O(log n) constraint. Not Monotonic Stack: Maintaining monotonic order tracks global mountain boundaries in O(n) space and time. Not Greedy: Pure local greedy steps without logarithmic search space halving take O(n) time.
